register: Neutral-formal historical and political term; putsch militaire is more vivid and often suggests a rapid seizure by a small armed group.
trap: Coup alone is too broad in French; the fixed political expression is coup d’État, with a capital É to denote the state as an institution.
example_tl: Le coup d’État militaire de 1973 a renversé le gouvernement élu, dissous le Parlement et installé durablement l’armée au cœur du pouvoir chilien.
example_en: The 1973 military coup overthrew the elected government, dissolved Parliament, and durably installed the armed forces at the heart of Chilean power.
cloze: {{c1::Le coup d’État militaire}} de 1973 a renversé le gouvernement élu, dissous le Parlement et installé durablement l’armée au cœur du pouvoir chilien.
note: Old_back gives the correct established term. Self-review retained militaire because it identifies the agent rather than merely repeating the violent character of a coup.

register: Standard historical and journalistic plural for individual guerrilla fighters; guérilla instead denotes the irregular force or form of warfare collectively.
trap: The legacy les guérillas changes people into organizations or campaigns; an individual fighter is un guérillero, feminine une guérillera.
example_tl: Les guérilleros contrôlaient les routes secondaires, mais dépendaient des villages voisins pour obtenir des renseignements, des vivres et des soins médicaux.
example_en: The guerrillas controlled the secondary roads but depended on neighboring villages for intelligence, provisions, and medical care.
cloze: {{c1::Les guérilleros}} contrôlaient les routes secondaires, mais dépendaient des villages voisins pour obtenir des renseignements, des vivres et des soins médicaux.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which uses the collective noun guérilla in the plural rather than naming the fighters intended by the English prompt.

register: Neutral term in history and political economy; surrounding prose determines whether it is descriptive, approving, or critical.
trap: Capitalisme names the economic system, while capitaliste can be an adjective or a person; French common names of doctrines remain lowercase.
example_tl: Les défenseurs du capitalisme soulignaient sa capacité d’adaptation, tandis que ses critiques estimaient qu’il ne réduisait pas les inégalités sociales.
example_en: Defenders of capitalism emphasized its capacity to adapt, while its critics argued that it did not reduce social inequalities.
cloze: Les défenseurs {{c1::du capitalisme}} soulignaient sa capacité d’adaptation, tandis que ses critiques estimaient qu’il ne réduisait pas les inégalités sociales.
note: Retained in COLD_WAR_VOCAB under the exact-duplicate report rather than in FANCY_VOCAB. Old_back is accurate; audit review attributed the contested assessment in the example.

register: Neutral-formal political term for a system or form of government, though an unmodified reference to a particular régime can sound critical.
trap: French régime is broader than dictatorship and can describe a democratic constitutional order; the accent also distinguishes it from English spelling.
example_tl: Le régime autorisait plusieurs partis, mais contrôlait leur financement, limitait leur accès aux médias et invalidait les candidatures jugées menaçantes.
example_en: The regime allowed several parties but controlled their funding, limited their access to the media, and disqualified candidacies deemed threatening.
cloze: {{c1::Le régime}} autorisait plusieurs partis, mais contrôlait leur financement, limitait leur accès aux médias et invalidait les candidatures jugées menaçantes.
note: Old_back supplies the correct headword. Self-review replaced annulait les candidatures with idiomatic invalidait and avoided falsely defining every régime as a dictatorship.

register: Neutral-formal political adjective for power that demands obedience and sharply limits pluralism or institutional accountability.
trap: The legacy l’autoritarisme is the noun authoritarianism, not the requested adjective; autoritaire can also describe a domineering person outside politics.
example_tl: Le gouvernement demeurait autoritaire malgré les élections, car l’opposition restait exclue des médias et les magistrats subissaient des pressions systématiques.
example_en: The government remained authoritarian despite the elections because the opposition was excluded from the media and judges faced systematic pressure.
cloze: Le gouvernement demeurait {{c1::autoritaire}} malgré les élections, car l’opposition restait exclue des médias et les magistrats subissaient des pressions systématiques.
note: Retained here under the exact-duplicate report. Materially corrects old_back’s part-of-speech error and restores lowercase for an isolated adjective.

register: Neutral-formal historical noun for forced or constrained residence outside one’s country; exil politique makes the cause explicit.
trap: Exil names the condition or displacement, whereas exilé names a person; the fixed phrase en exil normally has no article.
example_tl: L’exil a permis à certains opposants de poursuivre leur combat politique, tout en les éloignant des réseaux clandestins restés dans leur pays.
example_en: Exile enabled some opponents to continue their political struggle while distancing them from the clandestine networks that remained in their country.
cloze: {{c1::L’exil}} a permis à certains opposants de poursuivre leur combat politique, tout en les éloignant des réseaux clandestins restés dans leur pays.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary initial capitalization; the card supplies the productive exil/exilé and en exil distinctions.

register: Standard historical and journalistic term, usually critical, for a military leadership that has collectively seized political power.
trap: Unlike Spanish junta or Portuguese junta, French junte is not the ordinary word for a committee or board; it strongly evokes authoritarian rule.
example_tl: La junte militaire a suspendu la Constitution, interdit les syndicats et confié les principaux ministères à des officiers issus de l’état-major.
example_en: The military junta suspended the Constitution, banned trade unions, and entrusted the main ministries to officers from the general staff.
cloze: {{c1::La junte militaire}} a suspendu la Constitution, interdit les syndicats et confié les principaux ministères à des officiers issus de l’état-major.
note: Sharpens old_back by making the military scope explicit in the production headword; the shorter legacy form remains a valid contextual alternative.

register: Specialist military and security-policy term for the combined political, intelligence, policing, and military response to an insurgency.
trap: Contre-insurrection is broader than a single counterattack: it can include intelligence, propaganda, population control, development programs, and coercion.
example_tl: La contre-insurrection combinait opérations militaires, renseignement et contrôle des populations, au risque de confondre soutien civil et participation armée.
example_en: Counterinsurgency combined military operations, intelligence, and population control, at the risk of conflating civilian support with armed participation.
cloze: {{c1::La contre-insurrection}} combinait opérations militaires, renseignement et contrôle des populations, au risque de confondre soutien civil et participation armée.
note: Old_back is accurate; the example fixes the doctrine’s integrated scope rather than reducing it to combat against insurgents.

register: Official institutional name and French initialism; OEA is standard in diplomatic, historical, and journalistic prose.
trap: Do not carry over English OAS: French reorders the initials to OEA, matching Organisation des États américains.
example_tl: L’OEA a condamné officiellement le coup d’État, mais ses divisions internes ont empêché l’adoption rapide de mesures collectives contraignantes.
example_en: The OAS officially condemned the coup, but its internal divisions prevented the swift adoption of binding collective measures.
cloze: {{c1::L’OEA}} a condamné officiellement le coup d’État, mais ses divisions internes ont empêché l’adoption rapide de mesures collectives contraignantes.
note: Old_back correctly localizes both the official name and its acronym. The cloze tests the acronym actually used in the contextual sentence.

register: Established international-relations term for conflicts in which outside powers support local belligerents instead of fighting one another directly.
trap: The fixed phrase is par procuration, not a literal guerre de procuration; it foregrounds outside sponsorship without erasing local actors’ own aims.
example_tl: Les guerres par procuration ont permis aux superpuissances de s’opposer sans s’affronter directement, en transférant aux sociétés locales l’essentiel des destructions.
example_en: Proxy wars allowed the superpowers to oppose one another without fighting directly, transferring most of the destruction to local societies.
cloze: {{c1::Les guerres par procuration}} ont permis aux superpuissances de s’opposer sans s’affronter directement, en transférant aux sociétés locales l’essentiel des destructions.
note: Old_back gives the established French term. Self-review removed a lexical contradiction around confrontation and preserved local societies’ agency.

register: Neutral-formal term for the conduct of relations and negotiation between political entities; it can denote both a practice and an institutional field.
trap: Diplomatie is the practice or field, diplomate is a person, and diplomatique is the adjective; these forms are not interchangeable.
example_tl: La diplomatie a maintenu des canaux discrets entre les blocs, même lorsque les déclarations publiques excluaient tout compromis sur les missiles.
example_en: Diplomacy maintained discreet channels between the blocs even when public statements ruled out any compromise over the missiles.
cloze: {{c1::La diplomatie}} a maintenu des canaux discrets entre les blocs, même lorsque les déclarations publiques excluaient tout compromis sur les missiles.
note: Retained in COLD_WAR_VOCAB under the exact-duplicate report rather than in FANCY_VOCAB. Old_back is accurate.

register: Formal trade-policy term covering tariffs and non-tariff measures; barrières commerciales is common, while obstacles au commerce is especially clear institutionally.
trap: The concept is broader than tariffs: quotas, licensing, discriminatory standards, and administrative procedures can also constitute obstacles au commerce.
example_tl: Les obstacles au commerce ont protégé certaines industries nationales, mais également accru le coût des équipements importés dont dépendait la modernisation économique.
example_en: Trade barriers protected certain domestic industries but also increased the cost of imported equipment on which economic modernization depended.
cloze: {{c1::Les obstacles au commerce}} ont protégé certaines industries nationales, mais également accru le coût des équipements importés dont dépendait la modernisation économique.
note: Reorders old_back into the clearer institutional collocation obstacles au commerce. Self-review replaced a debatable transitive use of renchérir with accru le coût.

register: Neutral-formal media, political, and legal term for suppressing or prohibiting information, expression, or publication.
trap: English censorship is French censure, but English censure meaning formal condemnation is blâme or condamnation; the apparent cognate reverses the learner’s expectation.
example_tl: La censure empêchait les journaux de faire état des arrestations arbitraires, tandis que la radio officielle attribuait toute contestation à des agents étrangers.
example_en: Censorship prevented newspapers from reporting arbitrary arrests, while official radio attributed all dissent to foreign agents.
cloze: {{c1::La censure}} empêchait les journaux de faire état des arrestations arbitraires, tandis que la radio officielle attribuait toute contestation à des agents étrangers.
note: Retained here under the exact-duplicate report. Self-review replaced translation-like publier les arrestations with idiomatic faire état des arrestations; old_back incorrectly capitalizes the noun.

register: Established but contested term in political economy; careful prose should specify the policies, institutions, or historical project being described.
trap: French libéralisme commonly foregrounds market economics, unlike liberalism in contemporary U.S. politics; néolibéralisme is not simply a newer form of social liberalism.
example_tl: Le néolibéralisme a redéfini le rôle de l’État sans le réduire, en mobilisant ses institutions pour ouvrir des secteurs publics à la concurrence.
example_en: Neoliberalism redefined the role of the state without reducing it, mobilizing its institutions to open public sectors to competition.
cloze: {{c1::Le néolibéralisme}} a redéfini le rôle de l’État sans le réduire, en mobilisant ses institutions pour ouvrir des secteurs publics à la concurrence.
note: Retained in COLD_WAR_VOCAB under the exact-duplicate report rather than in FANCY_VOCAB. Old_back is accurate.

register: Established Cold War history and international-relations term for the U.S. strategy of limiting further Soviet expansion rather than overthrowing the Soviet state.
trap: In this doctrine, containment is endiguement, not confinement or contention; politique d’endiguement makes the geopolitical sense explicit.
example_tl: La politique d’endiguement visait moins à renverser l’Union soviétique qu’à freiner l’expansion de son influence par des alliances et des aides ciblées.
example_en: The policy of containment aimed less to overthrow the Soviet Union than to curb the expansion of its influence through alliances and targeted aid.
cloze: {{c1::La politique d’endiguement}} visait moins à renverser l’Union soviétique qu’à freiner l’expansion de son influence par des alliances et des aides ciblées.
note: Sharpens old_back by promoting the full doctrinal label politique d’endiguement; the shorter endiguement remains natural when Cold War context is already explicit.

register: Neutral-formal geopolitical label for groups aligned with or supportive of U.S. policy; it does not necessarily imply direct control by Washington.
trap: The prefix pro- expresses support or alignment; in the standard closed spelling proaméricain, the adjective agrees normally: factions proaméricaines.
example_tl: Les factions proaméricaines recevaient des armes et un soutien financier, sans pour autant partager l’ensemble des priorités stratégiques de Washington.
example_en: The pro-U.S. factions received weapons and financial support without necessarily sharing all of Washington’s strategic priorities.
cloze: {{c1::Les factions proaméricaines}} recevaient des armes et un soutien financier, sans pour autant partager l’ensemble des priorités stratégiques de Washington.
note: Standardizes legacy pro-américaines to the closed dictionary spelling proaméricaines. Self-review states alignment without inferring that the factions were mere proxies.

register: Historical and human-rights plural for people abducted or detained whose fate and whereabouts are deliberately concealed by state agents or their allies.
trap: A disparu can simply be a missing person; the Cold War term les disparus invokes enforced disappearance, and the legacy feminine adjective lacks the required article.
example_tl: Les disparus figuraient rarement dans les registres officiels, tandis que leurs familles cherchaient une trace vérifiable dans les prisons, les casernes et les archives.
example_en: The disappeared rarely appeared in official registers, while their families searched for a verifiable trace in prisons, barracks, and archives.
cloze: {{c1::Les disparus}} figuraient rarement dans les registres officiels, tandis que leurs familles cherchaient une trace vérifiable dans les prisons, les casernes et les archives.
note: The Cold War context supports the substantivized plural the disappeared, materially correcting old_back. Self-review replaced the literary bare-noun list with natural prepositional phrasing.

register: Neutral-formal international-relations term for coercive restrictions on trade, finance, assets, or transactions imposed to change an actor’s conduct.
trap: French sanctionner can exceptionally mean to ratify or approve in formal institutional usage; sanctions économiques unambiguously denotes coercive penalties.
example_tl: Les sanctions économiques ont réduit les recettes d’exportation du régime, mais leurs effets ont surtout pesé sur les ménages privés de médicaments importés.
example_en: Economic sanctions reduced the regime’s export revenue, but their effects fell mainly on households deprived of imported medicines.
cloze: {{c1::Les sanctions économiques}} ont réduit les recettes d’exportation du régime, mais leurs effets ont surtout pesé sur les ménages privés de médicaments importés.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. The card records the narrower coercive sense selected by the international-relations context.

register: Established historical proper name for the French resistance movements of the Second World War; lowercase résistance is the generic common noun.
trap: Capitalization carries meaning: la Résistance denotes the historical movements, whereas la résistance can describe opposition to any occupier, regime, or policy.
example_tl: La Résistance a survécu dans la mémoire politique d’après-guerre comme un héritage disputé, mobilisé aussi bien par les gaullistes que par les communistes.
example_en: The Resistance endured in postwar political memory as a contested legacy, invoked by Gaullists and Communists alike.
cloze: {{c1::La Résistance}} a survécu dans la mémoire politique d’après-guerre comme un héritage disputé, mobilisé aussi bien par les gaullistes que par les communistes.
note: Old_back has the right term and capitalization. Self-review fixed the example to the specifically French historical sense signaled by the source capital.

register: Neutral academic and political noun; it can become critical when it implies a rigid or distorting system of ideas.
trap: French idéologie is not automatically pejorative, and common names of doctrines and schools of thought normally remain lowercase.
example_tl: L’idéologie structurait les alliances bien au-delà des intérêts immédiats, en imposant aux gouvernements une lecture binaire de chaque crise régionale.
example_en: Ideology structured alliances far beyond immediate interests by imposing a binary reading of every regional crisis on governments.
cloze: {{c1::L’idéologie}} structurait les alliances bien au-delà des intérêts immédiats, en imposant aux gouvernements une lecture binaire de chaque crise régionale.
note: Retained in COLD_WAR_VOCAB under the exact-duplicate report rather than in FANCY_VOCAB; old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization.

register: Established neutral-formal term in strategic studies and modern history, applicable to both nuclear and conventional weapons competition.
trap: The fixed complement is aux armements; neither a literal course des armes nor the narrower course aux armes is idiomatic for this geopolitical concept.
example_tl: La course aux armements a absorbé des ressources considérables, tout en alimentant une insécurité que chaque nouveau missile prétendait précisément réduire.
example_en: The arms race absorbed considerable resources while fueling an insecurity that each new missile purported precisely to reduce.
cloze: {{c1::La course aux armements}} a absorbé des ressources considérables, tout en alimentant une insécurité que chaque nouveau missile prétendait précisément réduire.
note: Old_back gives the established expression. Self-review removed a looser singular variant because it is less canonical and not freely interchangeable.

register: Political-science term, often critical; context must show whether it concerns state action in the economy or intervention in another country.
trap: French interventionnisme has two consecutive n letters and names a doctrine or systematic policy, not merely one intervention ponctuelle.
example_tl: L’interventionnisme de Washington en Amérique latine associait aide économique, pression diplomatique et opérations clandestines afin de contenir les gouvernements jugés hostiles.
example_en: Washington’s interventionism in Latin America combined economic aid, diplomatic pressure, and covert operations to contain governments deemed hostile.
cloze: {{c1::L’interventionnisme}} de Washington en Amérique latine associait aide économique, pression diplomatique et opérations clandestines afin de contenir les gouvernements jugés hostiles.
note: Old_back is correct. Self-review made the foreign-policy sense explicit because the same French noun also denotes domestic economic interventionism.

register: Historical party label in the Chilean context; lowercase la démocratie chrétienne instead names the broader political tradition.
trap: Do not transfer Italian title capitalization mechanically: the generic current is la démocratie chrétienne, while the Chilean party is also called le Parti démocrate-chrétien.
example_tl: La Démocratie chrétienne chilienne a porté un projet réformiste qui modernisait l’agriculture sans remettre entièrement en cause les structures de propriété.
example_en: Chilean Christian Democracy pursued a reformist project that modernized agriculture without entirely challenging property structures.
cloze: {{c1::La Démocratie chrétienne}} chilienne a porté un projet réformiste qui modernisait l’agriculture sans remettre entièrement en cause les structures de propriété.
note: Interprets the capitalized source within the surrounding Chilean sequence as a party label; the generic tradition is la démocratie chrétienne. Self-review removed a gender-changing alternative and replaced a contestable junta claim with the party’s documented agrarian-policy context.

register: Neutral-formal term in agrarian history and development policy, specifically referring to the transfer or reallocation of landholdings.
trap: Redistribution des terres is narrower than réforme agraire, which can also encompass credit, tenure rules, cooperatives, and rural infrastructure.
example_tl: La redistribution des terres promise par le gouvernement menaçait les grands propriétaires, mais son application inégale déçut rapidement les communautés rurales.
example_en: The land redistribution promised by the government threatened large landowners, but its uneven implementation quickly disappointed rural communities.
cloze: {{c1::La redistribution des terres}} promise par le gouvernement menaçait les grands propriétaires, mais son application inégale déçut rapidement les communautés rurales.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained this item alongside agrarian reform because it denotes the narrower transfer mechanism, not the whole reform program.

register: Neutral-formal legal and political-economy term for a compulsory taking; historical accounts may use it without endorsing the measure’s legality.
trap: In legal French, expropriation normally invokes public purpose and compensation; confiscation denotes a punitive taking and is not a neutral synonym.
example_tl: L’expropriation des compagnies minières devait transférer leurs actifs à l’État, sous réserve d’une indemnisation dont le calcul provoqua un conflit diplomatique.
example_en: The expropriation of the mining companies was to transfer their assets to the state, subject to compensation whose calculation caused a diplomatic conflict.
cloze: {{c1::L’expropriation}} des compagnies minières devait transférer leurs actifs à l’État, sous réserve d’une indemnisation dont le calcul provoqua un conflit diplomatique.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review kept the legal distinction from confiscation explicit rather than treating the two as stylistic alternatives.

register: Standard in social and agrarian history; in contemporary occupational reporting, agriculteurs is usually more neutral and institutionally precise.
trap: Paysan need not carry the contemptuous force of English peasant, but it frames people as a rural social group rather than simply as farm operators.
example_tl: Les paysans se sont mobilisés lorsque la réforme agraire a cessé d’être une promesse abstraite pour modifier concrètement la répartition des terres.
example_en: The peasants mobilized when agrarian reform ceased to be an abstract promise and began concretely changing the distribution of land.
cloze: {{c1::Les paysans}} se sont mobilisés lorsque la réforme agraire a cessé d’être une promesse abstraite pour modifier concrètement la répartition des terres.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review rejected agriculteurs because it loses the historical class framing, then replaced rejoindre les mobilisations with the more idiomatic se mobiliser.

register: Neutral-formal term for a firm, confrontational disposition in political, trade-union, or social action; it can be rhetorical and does not necessarily imply violence.
trap: French militantisme usually denotes organized activism and is weaker than English militancy when the latter foregrounds a combative posture.
example_tl: La combativité du syndicat s’est accrue après l’échec des négociations, bien que ses dirigeants aient continué de rejeter explicitement la violence politique.
example_en: The union's militancy increased after negotiations failed, although its leaders continued explicitly to reject political violence.
cloze: {{c1::La combativité}} du syndicat s’est accrue après l’échec des négociations, bien que ses dirigeants aient continué de rejeter explicitement la violence politique.
note: Materially corrects the false-friend legacy rendering: French militantisme normally means organized activism, whereas the English prompt foregrounds a combative posture.

register: Established neutral-formal term in rural history and development policy, broader than the redistribution of land alone.
trap: English agrarian corresponds here to French agraire, not agrarien, which chiefly describes an ideology or a partisan of agrarian interests.
example_tl: La réforme agraire visait non seulement à morceler les grands domaines, mais aussi à élargir l’accès au crédit et aux infrastructures rurales.
example_en: Agrarian reform aimed not only to break up the large estates but also to broaden access to credit and rural infrastructure.
cloze: {{c1::La réforme agraire}} visait non seulement à morceler les grands domaines, mais aussi à élargir l’accès au crédit et aux infrastructures rurales.
note: Kept as the canonical singular specialist term; the plural land reforms item 043 was dropped as a constructional duplicate.

register: Standard neutral plural in labor, political, and journalistic contexts; organisations syndicales is a slightly more institutional alternative.
trap: English trade union is syndicat, not union commerciale; French union more often names a union or federation explicitly bearing that word in its title.
example_tl: Les syndicats ont coordonné une grève nationale malgré l’état d’urgence, transformant des revendications professionnelles en épreuve politique pour le gouvernement.
example_en: The trade unions coordinated a nationwide strike despite the state of emergency, turning workplace demands into a political test for the government.
cloze: {{c1::Les syndicats}} ont coordonné une grève nationale malgré l’état d’urgence, transformant des revendications professionnelles en épreuve politique pour le gouvernement.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review limited the alternative to a genuinely interchangeable institutional phrase rather than adding the narrower syndicats de salariés.

register: Standard policy and social-science usage; the plural normally denotes measurable disparities, while singular l’inégalité is more abstract or theoretical.
trap: Do not preserve English singular mechanically: French policy prose usually discusses les inégalités when referring to gaps in income, status, or access.
example_tl: Les inégalités se sont creusées malgré la croissance, car les gains de productivité ont surtout profité aux groupes déjà proches du pouvoir.
example_en: Inequalities widened despite growth because productivity gains mainly benefited groups that were already close to power.
cloze: {{c1::Les inégalités}} se sont creusées malgré la croissance, car les gains de productivité ont surtout profité aux groupes déjà proches du pouvoir.
note: Old_back’s plural is idiomatic for the policy sense. Self-review retained it rather than forcing source-number symmetry with the more abstract l’inégalité.

register: Neutral, invariable adjective phrase used after a noun to describe political alignment; suitable in both journalism and academic prose.
trap: The legacy Gauche is a capitalized noun, not the requested adjective; ordinary ideological uses of de gauche take no capital letter.
example_tl: Les partis de gauche défendaient la nationalisation du cuivre, mais divergeaient profondément sur le rythme des réformes et le recours à la mobilisation populaire.
example_en: Left-wing parties supported nationalizing copper but differed profoundly over the pace of reforms and recourse to popular mobilization.
cloze: Les partis {{c1::de gauche}} défendaient la nationalisation du cuivre, mais divergeaient profondément sur le rythme des réformes et le recours à la mobilisation populaire.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which supplies the noun gauche and changes the source’s part of speech.

register: Neutral political and journalistic term for sustained collective challenge; protestation more often denotes a discrete objection or public statement.
trap: French manifestation is a street demonstration, not the whole phenomenon of protest; contestation can also include strikes, occupations, publications, and boycotts.
example_tl: La contestation étudiante a débordé les campus lorsque la police a interdit les rassemblements et que les journaux ont minimisé les violences.
example_en: Student protest spread beyond the campuses when police banned gatherings and newspapers played down the violence.
cloze: {{c1::La contestation}} étudiante a débordé les campus lorsque la police a interdit les rassemblements et que les journaux ont minimisé les violences.
note: Diverges from old_back: contestation better captures sustained political protest, whereas protestation remains possible for a discrete objection or public statement.

register: Formal political and intellectual term, especially for opposition expressed under a dominant doctrine or authoritarian system.
trap: English dissent can be an ordinary désaccord; French dissidence implies a more consequential break with an authority, party line, or governing orthodoxy.
example_tl: La dissidence intellectuelle s’exprimait dans des revues clandestines, dont chaque exemplaire franchissait les frontières au prix de risques considérables pour les rédacteurs.
example_en: Intellectual dissent found expression in clandestine journals, each copy of which crossed borders at considerable risk to the editors.
cloze: {{c1::La dissidence}} intellectuelle s’exprimait dans des revues clandestines, dont chaque exemplaire franchissait les frontières au prix de risques considérables pour les rédacteurs.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review kept the stronger political sense and replaced circulait par des revues with the idiomatic s’exprimait dans des revues.

register: Proper historical name of the Chilean left-wing coalition associated with Salvador Allende; the original Spanish name also occurs in French scholarship.
trap: Capitalize Unité when naming the coalition; lowercase unité populaire is merely a generic phrase meaning popular unity.
example_tl: L’Unité populaire rassemblait socialistes, communistes et autres forces de gauche autour d’un programme de transformations institutionnelles porté par Salvador Allende.
example_en: Popular Unity brought together Socialists, Communists, and other left-wing forces around a program of institutional transformations championed by Salvador Allende.
cloze: {{c1::L’Unité populaire}} rassemblait socialistes, communistes et autres forces de gauche autour d’un programme de transformations institutionnelles porté par Salvador Allende.
note: Materially corrects old_back by restoring the historical coalition’s capitalization; self-review replaced the less idiomatic programme conduit with programme porté.

register: Formal economics and finance term for reducing investment or disposing of assets; retrait des capitaux is more explicit in a cross-border context.
trap: Désengagement is broader and can be political or military, while cession names a sale; neither automatically conveys the reduction of invested capital.
example_tl: Le désinvestissement étranger s’est accéléré après les nationalisations, privant le pays de capitaux au moment même où ses besoins industriels augmentaient.
example_en: Foreign divestment accelerated after the nationalizations, depriving the country of capital just as its industrial needs were increasing.
cloze: {{c1::Le désinvestissement}} étranger s’est accéléré après les nationalisations, privant le pays de capitaux au moment même où ses besoins industriels augmentaient.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review excluded désengagement because it is broader than the financial sense and removed retrait des capitaux because clean substitution would require moving the example’s adjective.

register: Neutral-formal institutional term for a government’s external relationships; relations internationales is broader and also names the academic field.
trap: Avoid the English calque relations étrangères; French normally uses relations extérieures for an institution’s external affairs or relations internationales more broadly.
example_tl: Les relations extérieures du gouvernement se sont dégradées après l’expropriation des entreprises américaines et le rapprochement diplomatique avec Cuba.
example_en: The government’s foreign relations deteriorated after the expropriation of American companies and the diplomatic rapprochement with Cuba.
cloze: {{c1::Les relations extérieures}} du gouvernement se sont dégradées après l’expropriation des entreprises américaines et le rapprochement diplomatique avec Cuba.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained relations internationales because it remains idiomatic in the example, while noting its broader possible scope.

register: Specialist economics and political-science term for a state-led development doctrine; développementisme is a less common but established variant.
trap: Développementalisme names a doctrine or policy model, not development itself; le développement and l’aide au développement are therefore not synonyms.
example_tl: Les partisans du développementalisme brésilien mettaient en avant la planification étatique et l’industrialisation rapide, tandis que ses critiques jugeaient l’autonomie économique promise encore inachevée.
example_en: Supporters of Brazilian developmentalism emphasized state planning and rapid industrialization, while its critics considered the promised economic autonomy still unrealized.
cloze: Les partisans {{c1::du développementalisme}} brésilien mettaient en avant la planification étatique et l’industrialisation rapide, tandis que ses critiques jugeaient l’autonomie économique promise encore inachevée.
note: Old_back gives the accepted headword. Self-review retained développementisme only as an established variant and made the doctrine, rather than generic development, explicit. Audit review attributed the contested assessment in the example.

register: Specialist development-economics term; the longer alternative explicitly names the industrialization strategy built around the policy.
trap: The established complement is aux importations, not the legacy des importations; the policy replaces imported goods with domestic production rather than merely restricting imports.
example_tl: La substitution aux importations devait réduire la dépendance extérieure du Brésil, mais elle exigeait des équipements et des technologies encore achetés à l’étranger.
example_en: Import substitution was intended to reduce Brazil’s external dependence, but it required equipment and technologies that were still purchased abroad.
cloze: {{c1::La substitution aux importations}} devait réduire la dépendance extérieure du Brésil, mais elle exigeait des équipements et des technologies encore achetés à l’étranger.
note: Materially corrects old_back’s nonstandard substitution des importations. Self-review checked that the longer alternative remains grammatical and equivalent in the example.

en: Tropicalia (referring to the music and art movement)
register: Established cultural-history name for the Brazilian movement of the late 1960s; tropicalisme is the usual French descriptive alternative.
trap: Preserve the Portuguese accent in Tropicália; tropical names a climate or style and does not by itself name this Brazilian movement.
example_tl: Le mouvement Tropicália a mêlé avant-garde, culture populaire et guitares électriques, transformant l’expérimentation musicale en critique indirecte de la dictature brésilienne.
example_en: The Tropicália movement blended the avant-garde, popular culture, and electric guitars, turning musical experimentation into an indirect critique of Brazil’s dictatorship.
cloze: {{c1::Le mouvement Tropicália}} a mêlé avant-garde, culture populaire et guitares électriques, transformant l’expérimentation musicale en critique indirecte de la dictature brésilienne.
note: Old_back explains the referent but does not supply a clean headword. Self-review used mouvement Tropicália to avoid uncertain article use before the bare proper name.

register: Neutral-formal adjective for activity deliberately concealed because it is prohibited or dangerous; frequent in political and resistance history.
trap: Old_back changes the adjective into the abstract noun clandestinité; French adjectives must agree, as in un réseau clandestin and une revue clandestine.
example_tl: Des journaux clandestins circulaient entre les universités malgré la censure, reliant les opposants exilés aux réseaux de résistance restés dans le pays.
example_en: Clandestine newspapers circulated among the universities despite censorship, linking exiled opponents with resistance networks that remained inside the country.
cloze: Des journaux {{c1::clandestins}} circulaient entre les universités malgré la censure, reliant les opposants exilés aux réseaux de résistance restés dans le pays.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which supplies a noun and therefore changes the source’s part of speech.

register: Neutral journalistic and economic plural for owners or senior figures in industry; context normally identifies the sector or political role.
trap: Les industriels denotes industrial business leaders or firms in this sense, not industrial workers, who are les ouvriers de l’industrie or les travailleurs de l’industrie.
example_tl: Une partie des industriels a soutenu le coup d’État lorsque les réformes sociales lui ont paru menacer ses investissements et son influence sur le gouvernement.
example_en: Some industrialists supported the coup when the social reforms appeared to threaten their investments and their influence over the government.
cloze: Une partie des {{c1::industriels}} a soutenu le coup d’État lorsque les réformes sociales lui ont paru menacer ses investissements et son influence sur le gouvernement.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained the business-leader sense but narrowed the example from all industrialists to une partie des industriels to avoid an overbroad historical claim.

register: Neutral-formal political and historical term for rule by the armed forces; pouvoir militaire emphasizes the authority they exercise.
trap: Gouvernance militaire is an awkward English calque for military rule and may instead suggest administrative methods; gouvernement militaire more narrowly names the executive.
example_tl: Le régime militaire a centralisé les décisions économiques tout en confiant leur mise en œuvre à une technocratie soucieuse de rassurer les investisseurs étrangers.
example_en: The military regime centralized economic decisions while entrusting their implementation to a technocracy eager to reassure foreign investors.
cloze: {{c1::Le régime militaire}} a centralisé les décisions économiques tout en confiant leur mise en œuvre à une technocratie soucieuse de rassurer les investisseurs étrangers.
note: Materially diverges from old_back: the surrounding Cold War sequence selects military rule, for which régime militaire is more idiomatic than gouvernance militaire.

register: Standard geographical name for the Amazon region or basin; the descriptive alternative is useful when territorial scope needs emphasis.
trap: French distinguishes l’Amazonie, the region, from l’Amazone, the river; the Brazilian development context selects the former.
example_tl: L’Amazonie est devenue un front d’expansion économique où routes, mines et élevage ont accéléré la déforestation au nom de l’intégration nationale.
example_en: The Amazon became a frontier of economic expansion where roads, mines, and cattle farming accelerated deforestation in the name of national integration.
cloze: {{c1::L’Amazonie}} est devenue un front d’expansion économique où routes, mines et élevage ont accéléré la déforestation au nom de l’intégration nationale.
note: Old_back correctly resolves the English ambiguity in favor of the region. Self-review retained an alternative that preserves that regional sense.

register: Established proper name of the Brazilian film movement that emerged around the turn of the 1960s; standard in film criticism and cultural history.
trap: Keep the Portuguese movement name untranslated and without a French accent on Cinema; nouveau cinéma or Nouvelle Vague would name different concepts.
example_tl: Le Cinema Novo a placé la pauvreté et les rapports de pouvoir au centre d’une esthétique cinématographique affranchie des modèles commerciaux dominants.
example_en: Cinema Novo placed poverty and power relations at the center of a cinematic aesthetic freed from dominant commercial models.
cloze: {{c1::Le Cinema Novo}} a placé la pauvreté et les rapports de pouvoir au centre d’une esthétique cinématographique affranchie des modèles commerciaux dominants.
note: Old_back adds a French common-noun article and capitalization that obscure the preserved Portuguese proper name. Self-review follows established French film usage, le Cinema Novo.

register: Neutral term in urban geography and policy for a city of exceptionally large population; exact thresholds depend on the analytical source.
trap: In precise geographical usage, mégalopole more often denotes a vast urbanized network comprising several metropolitan areas, not simply one megacity.
example_tl: São Paulo est devenue une mégapole dont l’expansion périphérique a dépassé les capacités de transport, de logement et d’assainissement des pouvoirs publics.
example_en: São Paulo became a megacity whose peripheral expansion outstripped the public authorities’ transport, housing, and sanitation capacity.
cloze: São Paulo est devenue une {{c1::mégapole}} dont l’expansion périphérique a dépassé les capacités de transport, de logement et d’assainissement des pouvoirs publics.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review avoided claiming a universal population threshold and retained the item for the useful mégapole versus mégalopole distinction.

register: Formal economics and political-history term for national economic self-sufficiency, whether pursued as a condition or a doctrine.
trap: Do not transfer Italian autarchia as *autarchie*: French has autarcie with c; autocratie instead concerns the concentration of political power.
example_tl: L’autarcie promise par le régime a surtout renchéri les biens d’équipement, sans supprimer la dépendance aux technologies et aux crédits étrangers.
example_en: The autarky promised by the regime mainly made capital goods more expensive, without eliminating dependence on foreign technologies and credit.
cloze: {{c1::L’autarcie}} promise par le régime a surtout renchéri les biens d’équipement, sans supprimer la dépendance aux technologies et aux crédits étrangers.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review replaced a generic cognate warning with the concrete Italian spelling interference and the autocratie distinction.

register: Established specialist term in development economics, sociology, and Latin American intellectual history.
trap: The fixed term contains the definite article de la; it analyzes structural center–periphery relations, not an individual state of personal dépendance.
example_tl: La théorie de la dépendance expliquait le sous-développement non comme un retard passager, mais comme le produit durable de relations économiques asymétriques.
example_en: Dependency theory explained underdevelopment not as a temporary lag but as the lasting product of asymmetrical economic relations.
cloze: {{c1::La théorie de la dépendance}} expliquait le sous-développement non comme un retard passager, mais comme le produit durable de relations économiques asymétriques.
note: Old_back gives the established term. Self-review made its structural analytical sense explicit rather than treating the phrase as merely compositional.

register: Standard Brazilian social-geography term in French; the singular is feminine, une favela, and the common noun is lowercase.
trap: Favela is not an exact synonym for every bidonville or quartier pauvre; it names a historically and institutionally specific Brazilian urban form.
example_tl: Les favelas ne forment pas un ensemble homogène : leur histoire, leur accès aux services publics et leurs relations avec l’État varient fortement.
example_en: Favelas do not form a homogeneous whole: their history, access to public services, and relations with the state vary greatly.
cloze: {{c1::Les favelas}} ne forment pas un ensemble homogène : leur histoire, leur accès aux services publics et leurs relations avec l’État varient fortement.
note: Old_back has the right loanword but unnecessary capitalization. Self-review used the plural requested by the source while stating the otherwise hidden feminine gender.

register: Specialist political-science adjective, especially associated with analyses of Latin American states and regimes under military rule.
trap: The compound is lowercase and hyphenated; both adjectival elements agree in the plural, as in des États bureaucratiques-autoritaires.
example_tl: L’État bureaucratique-autoritaire a exclu les classes populaires de la décision politique tout en confiant la stratégie économique à des experts civils et militaires.
example_en: The bureaucratic-authoritarian state excluded the popular classes from political decision-making while entrusting economic strategy to civilian and military experts.
cloze: L’État {{c1::bureaucratique-autoritaire}} a exclu les classes populaires de la décision politique tout en confiant la stratégie économique à des experts civils et militaires.
note: Old_back supplies the right specialist compound but incorrectly capitalizes an adjective. Self-review verified the established hyphenated political-science form.

register: Historical and political term for a personalist leader in Spain or Latin America; often critical in modern analytical prose.
trap: Lowercase caudillo is the generic noun and is narrower than dictateur; uppercase Caudillo specifically served as Franco’s title.
example_tl: Le caudillo consolidait son autorité grâce à des réseaux de fidélité personnelle, distribuant charges et ressources en échange d’un soutien qui contournait les institutions.
example_en: The caudillo consolidated his authority through networks of personal loyalty, distributing offices and resources in exchange for support that bypassed institutions.
cloze: {{c1::Le caudillo}} consolidait son autorité grâce à des réseaux de fidélité personnelle, distribuant charges et ressources en échange d’un soutien qui contournait les institutions.
note: Old_back has unnecessary capitalization for the generic Latin American sense. Self-review excluded dictateur and replaced par des fidélités with the idiomatic réseaux de fidélité personnelle.

register: Specialist political and institutional term; often historical or critical when describing state-managed representation of organized interests.
trap: Corporatisme is not the rule of commercial corporations: it organizes occupational interests into bodies recognized or controlled by the state.
example_tl: Le corporatisme regroupait patrons et salariés au sein d’organisations reconnues par l’État, afin de canaliser les conflits sociaux sans véritable pluralisme syndical.
example_en: Corporatism brought employers and employees together within state-recognized organizations in order to channel social conflicts without genuine trade-union pluralism.
cloze: {{c1::Le corporatisme}} regroupait patrons et salariés au sein d’organisations reconnues par l’État, afin de canaliser les conflits sociaux sans véritable pluralisme syndical.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review sharpened the commercial-corporation distinction and replaced the calqued organisait en groupes with regroupait au sein d’organisations.

register: Neutral-formal noun whose Cold War context selects systematic monitoring by police or intelligence services rather than benign supervision.
trap: French surveillance is broader than English surveillance and can mean ordinary supervision; administrative oversight may instead require contrôle or supervision depending on context.
example_tl: La surveillance des universitaires s’est étendue aux appels téléphoniques et au courrier, transformant toute critique du régime en indice potentiel de subversion.
example_en: Surveillance of university academics extended to telephone calls and mail, turning any criticism of the regime into potential evidence of subversion.
cloze: {{c1::La surveillance}} des universitaires s’est étendue aux appels téléphoniques et au courrier, transformant toute critique du régime en indice potentiel de subversion.
note: Retained in COLD_WAR_VOCAB under the exact-duplicate report rather than in FANCY_VOCAB; old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization.

register: Standard feminine genre name; bossa-nova is the traditional dictionary spelling, while the joined 1990 spelling bossanova is also accepted.
trap: Unlike Portuguese bossa nova, the traditional French spelling uses a hyphen; as a genre name it is feminine and normally lowercase.
example_tl: La bossa-nova a projeté une image raffinée du Brésil urbain, tandis que ses harmonies circulaient bien au-delà des publics lusophones.
example_en: Bossa nova projected a sophisticated image of urban Brazil, while its harmonies circulated far beyond Portuguese-speaking audiences.
cloze: {{c1::La bossa-nova}} a projeté une image raffinée du Brésil urbain, tandis que ses harmonies circulaient bien au-delà des publics lusophones.
note: Materially normalizes old_back’s capitalization and spacing. Self-review retained bossanova as the officially accepted rectified spelling and verified substitution in the example.

register: Established historical and journalistic label for rapid growth; often qualified or placed in quotation marks to signal its contested, selective framing.
trap: Miracle économique is an evaluative label, not a neutral statistical category; context should reveal whose gains, costs, and time frame are being described.
example_tl: Ce que le régime appelait le « miracle économique » a produit une expansion spectaculaire, mais des études ont montré que les gains profitaient surtout aux élites et dépendaient de l’endettement extérieur.
example_en: What the regime called the “economic miracle” produced spectacular expansion, but studies showed that the gains mainly benefited elites and depended on external debt.
cloze: Ce que le régime appelait le « {{c1::miracle économique}} » a produit une expansion spectaculaire, mais des études ont montré que les gains profitaient surtout aux élites et dépendaient de l’endettement extérieur.
note: Old_back gives the established phrase. Audit review attributed both the celebratory label and the later distributional assessment, while removing a repeated growth word family.

register: Neutral academic and journalistic singular denoting either the field or the power logic associated with a place, issue, or period.
trap: French normally uses singular géopolitique where awkward English may show geopolitics; géostratégie is narrower and is not a general synonym.
example_tl: La géopolitique de la guerre froide a souvent interprété les crises locales à travers le seul prisme de l’affrontement mondial entre les deux blocs.
example_en: Cold War geopolitics often interpreted local crises solely through the lens of the global confrontation between the two blocs.
cloze: {{c1::La géopolitique}} de la guerre froide a souvent interprété les crises locales à travers le seul prisme de l’affrontement mondial entre les deux blocs.
note: Retained in COLD_WAR_VOCAB under the exact-duplicate report rather than in FANCY_VOCAB; self-review replaced a literal réduire à leur position with the idiomatic à travers le prisme de.

register: Standard policy and development usage for roads, networks, and public facilities; singular l’infrastructure is more collective or conceptual.
trap: Do not preserve English collective singular automatically: French commonly uses les infrastructures when several physical networks or facilities are meant.
example_tl: Les infrastructures construites par le régime ont désenclavé de nouveaux territoires, mais elles ont aussi facilité l’exploitation intensive de ressources jusque-là difficiles d’accès.
example_en: The infrastructure built by the regime opened up new territories, but it also facilitated the intensive exploitation of previously hard-to-reach resources.
cloze: {{c1::Les infrastructures}} construites par le régime ont désenclavé de nouveaux territoires, mais elles ont aussi facilité l’exploitation intensive de ressources jusque-là difficiles d’accès.
note: Retained in COLD_WAR_VOCAB under the exact-duplicate report rather than in FANCY_VOCAB. Self-review changed the singular to the idiomatic policy plural and replaced the calqued intégrer des territoires with désenclaver.

register: Historical and demographic adjective or person label; its racializing history requires precise context and attention to people’s own identifications.
trap: Métissage names mixing as a process or condition, not a mestizo person or the adjective métis; gender is visible in the feminine form métisse.
example_tl: Le recensement a longtemps figé une population métisse dans des catégories raciales qui masquaient la diversité des trajectoires familiales et des appartenances revendiquées.
example_en: The census long confined a mixed-race population within racial categories that obscured the diversity of family histories and claimed identities.
cloze: Le recensement a longtemps figé une population {{c1::métisse}} dans des catégories raciales qui masquaient la diversité des trajectoires familiales et des appartenances revendiquées.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which gives the process noun métissage. The source is ambiguous between noun and adjective; this card teaches the adjective while the register line records the person-label use.

register: Neutral adjective in cultural, historical, and demographic writing; the specific noun it modifies should make the intended cultural or population reference clear.
trap: The prefix afro- is invariable, while brésilien agrees with the noun: cultures afro-brésiliennes; the ordinary adjective is lowercase and hyphenated.
example_tl: Les religions afro-brésiliennes ont préservé des cosmologies et des pratiques communautaires malgré la répression policière, les préjugés sociaux et les tentatives d’assimilation.
example_en: Afro-Brazilian religions preserved cosmologies and communal practices despite police repression, social prejudice, and attempts at assimilation.
cloze: Les religions {{c1::afro-brésiliennes}} ont préservé des cosmologies et des pratiques communautaires malgré la répression policière, les préjugés sociaux et les tentatives d’assimilation.
note: Old_back gives only the masculine singular and incorrectly capitalizes the adjective. Self-review made agreement explicit and tested the feminine plural in context.

register: Current neutral-formal institutional formula in international law and rights discourse, emphasizing peoples as collective rights holders.
trap: Indigène remains possible in some historical or scientific contexts, but droits des indigènes can sound reductive; autochtone is preferred in current institutional usage.
example_tl: Les droits des peuples autochtones ont été invoqués contre des projets miniers qui menaçaient leurs territoires, leurs ressources et leur autonomie politique.
example_en: Indigenous peoples’ rights were invoked against mining projects that threatened their territories, resources, and political autonomy.
cloze: {{c1::Les droits des peuples autochtones}} ont été invoqués contre des projets miniers qui menaçaient leurs territoires, leurs ressources et leur autonomie politique.
note: Materially updates old_back’s droits des indigènes to the current institutional formula. Self-review retained peuples because the example concerns collective territorial and political rights.

register: Specialist political-science term for an asymmetrical exchange of protection or resources for loyalty; the hyphenated alternative is also used in academic writing.
trap: Here patron is a political protector and client a dependent actor, not an employer and customer; relations entre patrons et clients would select the commercial sense.
example_tl: Les relations de clientèle ont permis à Moscou de conserver une influence décisive sur des régimes dépendants sans les administrer directement.
example_en: Patron-client relations allowed Moscow to retain decisive influence over dependent regimes without administering them directly.
cloze: {{c1::Les relations de clientèle}} ont permis à Moscou de conserver une influence décisive sur des régimes dépendants sans les administrer directement.
note: Old_back gives an accepted technical calque. Self-review selected relations de clientèle as the more idiomatic headword while retaining the established hyphenated form as an alternative.

register: Neutral environmental-policy phrase; en Amazonie locates the process, while de l’Amazonie presents the region as the forest area being depleted.
trap: Amazonie names the region, whereas Amazone names the river; the geographical construction normally uses en Amazonie, not dans l’Amazonie.
example_tl: La déforestation en Amazonie s’est accélérée lorsque le régime militaire a ouvert de nouveaux territoires à l’élevage, aux mines et à la spéculation foncière.
example_en: Deforestation in the Amazon accelerated when the military regime opened new territories to cattle farming, mining, and land speculation.
cloze: {{c1::La déforestation en Amazonie}} s’est accélérée lorsque le régime militaire a ouvert de nouveaux territoires à l’élevage, aux mines et à la spéculation foncière.
note: Old_back is possible, but self-review preferred en Amazonie because it unambiguously locates the process rather than suggesting the complete removal of the region’s forest.

register: Neutral-formal policy noun whose intended object should normally be made explicit, as in intégration régionale, économique, or nationale.
trap: English integration of X into Y is usually l’intégration de X à or dans Y; French learners should not reproduce the English sequence with en in every context.
example_tl: L’intégration régionale devait renforcer le poids diplomatique de l’Amérique latine, mais les rivalités nationales ont longtemps limité la portée des accords conclus.
example_en: Regional integration was intended to strengthen Latin America’s diplomatic weight, but national rivalries long limited the scope of the agreements reached.
cloze: {{c1::L’intégration}} régionale devait renforcer le poids diplomatique de l’Amérique latine, mais les rivalités nationales ont longtemps limité la portée des accords conclus.
note: Old_back is accurate. The exact-duplicate report assigns this source prompt to COLD_WAR_VOCAB rather than FANCY_VOCAB; self-review supplied a specific regional context to make the generic noun teachable.

tl: la maîtrise de la lecture et de l’écriture
register: Neutral educational and development-policy wording for the ability itself; taux d’alphabétisation is conventional when reporting a population statistic.
trap: Alphabétisation primarily names the teaching process or its statistical outcome, while littératie is a specialist term with uneven currency in France French.
example_tl: La maîtrise de la lecture et de l’écriture progressait, mais les écarts entre campagnes et villes continuaient de restreindre l’accès aux emplois qualifiés.
example_en: Literacy was improving, but disparities between rural and urban areas continued to restrict access to skilled jobs.
cloze: {{c1::La maîtrise de la lecture et de l’écriture}} progressait, mais les écarts entre campagnes et villes continuaient de restreindre l’accès aux emplois qualifiés.
note: Materially diverges from old_back, which gives the process alphabétisation rather than the underlying ability. Self-review retained the conventional statistical use only in the register guidance.

alts: la montée en puissance des évangéliques
register: Neutral journalistic and social-science phrase; the second alternative shifts the focus from the religious current to its adherents as political actors.
trap: Les évangéliques are evangelical believers, whereas les évangélistes are evangelists or preachers; the English adjective cannot be transferred mechanically.
example_tl: L’essor de l’évangélisme a reconfiguré le débat public brésilien, donnant à de nouvelles Églises un poids croissant dans les campagnes électorales.
example_en: The rise of evangelical Christianity reshaped Brazilian public debate, giving new churches growing weight in election campaigns.
cloze: {{c1::L’essor de l’évangélisme}} a reconfiguré le débat public brésilien, donnant à de nouvelles Églises un poids croissant dans les campagnes électorales.
note: Old_back is accurate but less idiomatic as a headword. Self-review chose essor and kept montée en puissance only with a human plural subject.

register: Neutral-formal education and development term for being unable to read or write; common in demographic measures such as taux d’analphabétisme.
trap: French distinguishes analphabétisme, never having learned to read and write, from illettrisme, seriously inadequate command after schooling.
example_tl: L’analphabétisme reculait dans les statistiques nationales, tandis que l’insuffisance des écoles rurales perpétuait de profondes inégalités entre les régions.
example_en: Illiteracy was declining in national statistics, while the inadequacy of rural schools perpetuated deep inequalities between regions.
cloze: {{c1::L’analphabétisme}} reculait dans les statistiques nationales, tandis que l’insuffisance des écoles rurales perpétuait de profondes inégalités entre les régions.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review added the institutionally useful distinction from illettrisme rather than treating the two terms as free synonyms.

register: Specialist human-geography phrase for the outward movement of settlement and exploitation into a previously less developed area.
trap: Expansion des frontières means enlargement of political borders; the Amazonian development process is the advance of a front pionnier.
example_tl: L’avancée du front pionnier en Amazonie a déplacé des communautés autochtones, fragmenté la forêt et renforcé l’emprise de grands propriétaires sur les terres.
example_en: Frontier expansion in the Amazon displaced Indigenous communities, fragmented the forest, and strengthened large landowners’ control over the land.
cloze: {{c1::L’avancée du front pionnier}} en Amazonie a déplacé des communautés autochtones, fragmenté la forêt et renforcé l’emprise de grands propriétaires sur les terres.
note: Materially corrects old_back, which describes a change in state borders. Self-review selected the established geographical concept front pionnier and an idiomatic collocation with avancée.

register: Standard diplomatic-history term for the easing of East–West tensions, especially from the 1960s to the late 1970s.
trap: In this domain détente is a historical diplomatic phase, not merely relaxation or reduced personal stress; English borrowed the French noun without its article.
example_tl: La détente a multiplié les canaux diplomatiques entre les deux blocs sans supprimer ni la compétition stratégique ni les conflits menés par alliés interposés.
example_en: Détente multiplied diplomatic channels between the two blocs without eliminating either strategic competition or conflicts waged through allied intermediaries.
cloze: {{c1::La détente}} a multiplié les canaux diplomatiques entre les deux blocs sans supprimer ni la compétition stratégique ni les conflits menés par alliés interposés.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review made the specialist historical sense explicit and avoided presenting détente as the end of Cold War competition.

register: Neutral-formal security and intelligence term for the covert acquisition of protected information on behalf of a state or organization.
trap: Espionnage names the activity, renseignement the information or intelligence field, and espion the person; these nouns are related but not interchangeable.
example_tl: L’espionnage industriel complétait les opérations militaires, car les technologies civiles pouvaient modifier rapidement l’équilibre stratégique entre les puissances rivales.
example_en: Industrial espionage supplemented military operations because civilian technologies could rapidly alter the strategic balance between rival powers.
cloze: {{c1::L’espionnage}} industriel complétait les opérations militaires, car les technologies civiles pouvaient modifier rapidement l’équilibre stratégique entre les puissances rivales.
note: Old_back is accurate. The exact-duplicate report assigns this prompt to COLD_WAR_VOCAB rather than FANCY_VOCAB; self-review distinguished the activity from renseignement.

register: Standard international-relations term for a conflict in which outside powers support local belligerents rather than confronting one another directly.
trap: The fixed construction is par procuration; old_back’s guerre des procurations incorrectly treats procuration as the object or participants of the war.
example_tl: La guerre par procuration permettait aux superpuissances d’armer leurs alliés régionaux tout en limitant le risque d’un affrontement militaire direct entre elles.
example_en: Proxy war allowed the superpowers to arm their regional allies while limiting the risk of a direct military confrontation between them.
cloze: {{c1::La guerre par procuration}} permettait aux superpuissances d’armer leurs alliés régionaux tout en limitant le risque d’un affrontement militaire direct entre elles.
note: Materially corrects old_back’s nonstandard plural construction. Self-review retained conflit par procuration as a true alternative when the armed confrontation is not formally called a war.

register: Established historical metaphor for the political, military, and ideological division between Soviet-dominated Eastern Europe and the West.
trap: French uses rideau, not the Italian cortina or a literal iron screen; the historical expression is normally lower-case in running text.
example_tl: Le rideau de fer a séparé des sociétés voisines, transformant les frontières européennes en dispositifs militaires, policiers et idéologiques presque infranchissables.
example_en: The Iron Curtain separated neighboring societies, turning European borders into military, police, and ideological systems that were almost impossible to cross.
cloze: {{c1::Le rideau de fer}} a séparé des sociétés voisines, transformant les frontières européennes en dispositifs militaires, policiers et idéologiques presque infranchissables.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review normalized the common-noun capitalization used in standard French prose.

register: Standard diplomatic and strategic-studies term; armements is the more institutional choice, while armes focuses more concretely on weapons.
trap: French says course aux armements, with à plus the plural article, rather than copying English word order as course nucléaire des armes.
example_tl: La course aux armements nucléaires a absorbé des ressources immenses et rendu chaque innovation défensive susceptible de provoquer une nouvelle escalade offensive.
example_en: The nuclear arms race absorbed immense resources and made each defensive innovation liable to provoke a new offensive escalation.
cloze: {{c1::La course aux armements nucléaires}} a absorbé des ressources immenses et rendu chaque innovation défensive susceptible de provoquer une nouvelle escalade offensive.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review kept armes nucléaires only as a slightly less institutional but contextually interchangeable alternative.

register: Established Cold War historical term for the claim that one country’s communist takeover would trigger similar changes in neighboring states.
trap: The established French name uses the plural des dominos, not the literal singular théorie du domino suggested by English’s attributive noun.
example_tl: La théorie des dominos a servi à présenter chaque victoire communiste locale comme le prélude mécanique à l’effondrement politique des États voisins.
example_en: The domino theory served to present each local communist victory as the mechanical prelude to the political collapse of neighboring states.
cloze: {{c1::La théorie des dominos}} a servi à présenter chaque victoire communiste locale comme le prélude mécanique à l’effondrement politique des États voisins.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review framed the theory as a historical claim rather than endorsing its causal assumptions.

register: Specialist nuclear-strategy term; French strategic writing commonly retains the memorable English acronym MAD after translating the phrase.
trap: Do not mechanically replace MAD with DMA: French institutional and strategic sources commonly retain the English acronym even beside the translated term.
example_tl: La destruction mutuelle assurée reposait sur la certitude qu’une première frappe déclencherait des représailles capables d’anéantir aussi l’agresseur.
example_en: Mutually assured destruction rested on the certainty that a first strike would trigger retaliation capable of annihilating the aggressor as well.
cloze: {{c1::La destruction mutuelle assurée}} reposait sur la certitude qu’une première frappe déclencherait des représailles capables d’anéantir aussi l’agresseur.
note: Old_back translates the phrase accurately. Self-review retained MAD because French diplomatic sources use that English acronym and kept it outside the clozed occurrence because the example does not spell it out.

register: Standard defense and strategic-studies term; the qualified alternative is useful when the context does not already establish a military doctrine.
trap: English deterrence is dissuasion in strategic French, not the nonexistent calque déterrence; découragement is a general effect rather than the doctrine.
example_tl: La dissuasion exigeait que l’adversaire croie à la capacité de riposte, mais aussi à la volonté politique d’y recourir effectivement.
example_en: Deterrence required the adversary to believe in both the capacity to retaliate and the political will actually to use it.
cloze: {{c1::La dissuasion}} exigeait que l’adversaire croie à la capacité de riposte, mais aussi à la volonté politique d’y recourir effectivement.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review avoided dissuasion nucléaire as an unqualified alternative because deterrence may also be conventional.

tl: le Mouvement des pays non alignés
register: Official name of the intergovernmental grouping in UN usage; the shorter alternative is an established historical and journalistic form.
trap: In the official form, pays is explicit and non alignés agrees with it; in the shorter form, les non-alignés is a substantivized plural and conventionally hyphenated.
example_tl: Le Mouvement des pays non alignés cherchait à préserver une autonomie diplomatique, même si ses membres divergeaient profondément sur leurs alliances et leurs modèles économiques.
example_en: The Non-Aligned Movement sought to preserve diplomatic autonomy, even though its members differed profoundly over their alliances and economic models.
cloze: {{c1::Le Mouvement des pays non alignés}} cherchait à préserver une autonomie diplomatique, même si ses membres divergeaient profondément sur leurs alliances et leurs modèles économiques.
note: Self-review replaced old_back’s common shorter form with the official UN name Mouvement des pays non alignés and retained Mouvement des non-alignés as an established alternative.

register: Neutral-formal but politically loaded term for a nominally sovereign state under another power’s decisive influence.
trap: Satellite follows the noun in French; it is not a literal celestial object here, and the plural is États satellites.
example_tl: Un État satellite conservait ses institutions nationales, mais ses choix stratégiques restaient étroitement subordonnés aux intérêts de la puissance tutélaire.
example_en: A satellite state retained its national institutions, but its strategic choices remained closely subordinated to the interests of the controlling power.
cloze: {{c1::Un État satellite}} conservait ses institutions nationales, mais ses choix stratégiques restaient étroitement subordonnés aux intérêts de la puissance tutélaire.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review used an indefinite article in the example because it defines a type rather than naming one particular state.

register: Standard international-relations term; zone d’influence is close but tends to evoke a more geographically bounded area.
trap: Sphère d’influence can include political, economic, or cultural leverage and is therefore broader than direct territorial control or formal sovereignty.
example_tl: Chaque superpuissance considérait sa sphère d’influence comme un espace réservé, où toute intervention adverse risquait d’être interprétée comme une provocation.
example_en: Each superpower regarded its sphere of influence as a reserved domain where any opposing intervention risked being interpreted as a provocation.
cloze: Chaque superpuissance considérait sa {{c1::sphère d’influence}} comme un espace réservé, où toute intervention adverse risquait d’être interprétée comme une provocation.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review removed zone d’influence from alts because its more bounded geographical scope makes it an explanatory near-synonym rather than a fully interchangeable answer.

register: Neutral-formal political and intelligence term for people who abandon one state, camp, or organization and join its adversary.
trap: A transfuge changes allegiance; a réfugié flees danger and a déserteur abandons military service, so neither is automatically a defector.
example_tl: Les transfuges fournissaient parfois des renseignements précieux, mais les services occidentaux redoutaient toujours qu’ils aient été envoyés pour diffuser de fausses informations.
example_en: Defectors sometimes provided valuable intelligence, but Western services always feared that they had been sent to spread false information.
cloze: {{c1::Les transfuges}} fournissaient parfois des renseignements précieux, mais les services occidentaux redoutaient toujours qu’ils aient été envoyés pour diffuser de fausses informations.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review excluded dissidents and refugees from the alternatives because opposition or flight alone does not entail a change of allegiance.

register: Standard security term for intelligence as collected and analyzed information or as a field of state activity; often singular in French.
trap: Intelligence is a false friend here: l’intelligence means intellectual ability or understanding, while an intelligence agency is un service de renseignement.
example_tl: Le renseignement reposait autant sur l’analyse patiente de sources ouvertes que sur les informations secrètes recueillies par des agents opérant clandestinement.
example_en: Intelligence relied as much on the patient analysis of open sources as on secret information collected by agents operating clandestinely.
cloze: {{c1::Le renseignement}} reposait autant sur l’analyse patiente de sources ouvertes que sur les informations secrètes recueillies par des agents opérant clandestinement.
note: Old_back correctly avoids the English false friend. Self-review kept the singular headword and explained the institutional construction separately.

register: Historical and political term for organized covert opposition; the alternative is broader and need not imply an armed or formally coordinated resistance.
trap: Le souterrain denotes an underground passage or something below ground; it does not name a clandestine political movement as English the underground can.
example_tl: La résistance clandestine diffusait des tracts, organisait des filières de fuite et maintenait un espace politique hors du contrôle du régime.
example_en: The underground distributed leaflets, organized escape networks, and maintained a political space beyond the regime’s control.
cloze: {{c1::La résistance clandestine}} diffusait des tracts, organisait des filières de fuite et maintenait un espace politique hors du contrôle du régime.
note: Materially corrects old_back’s physical sense. Self-review selected résistance clandestine for the organized political referent and changed the alternative to the grammatically interchangeable opposition clandestine.

register: Neutral-formal media, security, and political term for deliberately deceptive information or the operation that disseminates it.
trap: Désinformation implies an intention to deceive; it is narrower than information erronée, which may be false through mistake rather than manipulation.
example_tl: La désinformation soviétique exploitait des récits plausibles, relayés par des intermédiaires crédibles afin de dissimuler leur origine et d’influencer les opinions occidentales.
example_en: Soviet disinformation exploited plausible narratives relayed by credible intermediaries in order to conceal their origin and influence Western public opinion.
cloze: {{c1::La désinformation}} soviétique exploitait des récits plausibles, relayés par des intermédiaires crédibles afin de dissimuler leur origine et d’influencer les opinions occidentales.
note: Old_back is accurate. The exact-duplicate report assigns this prompt to COLD_WAR_VOCAB rather than FANCY_VOCAB; self-review made intentional deception central to the example.

register: Standard geography and security term for an intervening area intended to separate rival forces, territories, or systems.
trap: French forms the compound directly as zone tampon, without de; État tampon is a related term but names a sovereign polity rather than an area.
example_tl: Une zone tampon devait éloigner les forces rivales de la frontière, mais elle pouvait aussi limiter durablement la souveraineté des États concernés.
